parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
Hexene reacts with hydrogen gas to produce hexane.

reaction 1 $$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{(l)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}\text{(l)}$$

Fig. 3.1 shows the distribution of energies of $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ molecules at temperature $T$.

{{figure:figure_3_1.png}}

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Sketch on Fig. 3.1 the shape of the curve for the same sample of $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ molecules when the temperature is increased.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why increasing the temperature increases the rate of reaction 1.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: State the role of nickel when it is added to reaction 1.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
Annotate Fig. 3.2 to show the effect of adding nickel to reaction 1 at temperature $T$.

{{figure:figure_3_2.png}}

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Reaction 2 shows the equilibrium reaction between $\text{X(g)}$ and $\text{Y(g)}$ to produce $\text{Z(g)}$ in a sealed container.

reaction 2 $$a\text{X(g)} + b\text{Y(g)} \rightleftharpoons c\text{Z(g)}$$

Fig. 3.3 shows the effect of changing pressure on the percentage yield of $\text{Z(g)}$ at two different temperatures, $300\text{ K}$ and $350\text{ K}$.

{{figure:figure_3_3.png}}
parts.text: Deduce **two** conclusions about reaction 2 using Fig 3.3.
